newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador finance chief has served in troubled times.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador finance chief has served in troubled times.

text.p: New Ecuadorean Finance Minister Carlos Davalos is a lawyer and economist who has held many public posts, some during dark periods of the nation's past.
Davalos, 69, was most recently deputy director of the Radical Alfarist Front, the party of newly-appointed President Fabian Alarcon.
He also served as deputy secretary of finance during the Social Christian administration of Camilo Ponce Enriques from 1956 to 1960 and during the military dictatorship from 1972 to 1978.
He later served as financial advisor for President Rodrigo Borja, of the Democratic Leftist Party, who suspended Ecuador's debt payments.

Davalos, who was born in the coastal city of Guayaquil, studied law in Ecuador's Central University. He has also been director of the Organization of American States' Education Center of Public Administration.

Consulted by reporters about the future economic policy of Ecuador, Davalos said the new administration will first have to review the state of Ecuador's public finances, but suggested there might be changes to the economic plans of ousted President Abdala Bucaram.
